# Yardlet 0.11.14
## Security
- Keys and tokens in what the browser, session and terminal tools return are hidden in more cases.
## Another Mac's tasks
- File › Connect to Mac… lists the other Macs signed in to your Yardlet account with remote connections turned on, and connects to the one you choose without a number to confirm. You can sign in from there, and a connection link still works under Use a connection link. - When the other Mac runs an earlier Yardlet, or the account cannot approve the connection yet, you confirm a number on the other Mac or on a phone already connected to it, as before. - Settings › Yardlet Account says that Macs signed in to the same account can connect to this one.
## Conversation
- A Claude Code `/compact` that fails, whether you typed it or Yardlet ran it while the task was idle, shows as a failed compaction with Claude Code's reason, also after a relaunch. - The Settings window and the approval, question, plan and form cards share one set of text sizes, spacing and corners, and a form's labels, hints and "Required" are no longer small print.
## Antigravity
- A turn that Antigravity's plan limit stopped ends on a limit card with the reset time, as a Claude Code limit does, instead of showing the CLI's notice as the answer. - A turn that ended on the CLI's error notice ends as failed with its words, and a `run_agent` subagent that a limit or an error stopped ends as failed and says why. - Importing finds an Antigravity conversation in each folder it lists, and a conversation Yardlet started is listed only under the folder Yardlet opened it in.
## Fixes
- Keep tasks working with the lid closed turns on instead of saying Yardlet's helper is not available, and General › App shows Launch at login on a Mac where it was never turned on. - A Mac without a built-in lid (Mac mini, Mac Studio, iMac) no longer offers the lid setting.

# Yardlet 0.11.13
## Security
- Keys and tokens in what the browser, session and terminal tools return are hidden more reliably, and hiding them in a long result no longer holds up the window.
## Simulators
- A task's side panel has a Simulator tab, after Browser in its launcher and + menu. It shows an iOS simulator from your Xcode, an Android emulator from your Android SDK, or an Android phone or tablet that adb reaches, live, and you use it with the mouse, the trackpad and the keyboard. Yardlet starts devices without a window and changes nothing in Xcode's or the SDK's settings. - What the Mac lacks for a simulator (Xcode, an iOS runtime, the Android SDK) can be installed from the tab, which shows what it will download first. - Agents can see and drive the device their task attached, read its screen as elements, and hand it to you for a step only you can take. A device asks once before an agent first uses it, and a real Android device asks in each task. - The simulator helper runs in a sandbox, with no network. - Settings › General › Simulator turns it all off: the tabs close, the devices Yardlet started shut down, and Yardlet offers to remove what it installed.
## Conversation
- Pictures an answer's Markdown names are drawn in place, and videos and sounds play where they are named. A picture on the web loads only when you click Load image. - Mermaid blocks are drawn as diagrams, as in the Codex and Claude apps. - Codex's inline visualizations are drawn in the conversation, as in the Codex app. Claude Code and ACP agents get a `show_widget` tool that draws a view under its call. - A waiting approval, question or plan sits right above the composer on a panel of its own, as in the Claude app, and the composer stays free to type in. An answered request stays in its turn as one quiet line that names what was asked. - A message you send while an agent waits on you goes to the agent and answers what it waited on, instead of waiting until you press Decline. - A request's wider allows share one Always allow button, with each scope in its menu. - A task waiting on you reads Needs approval or Needs answer in the sidebar and home, and in the task only the progress line is orange. A split pane's outline marks focus alone. - Korean wraps between words in text fields and answers, and the composer grows while an input method is still composing a word. - In a narrow composer the model control shortens first, so Send stays in view. - A 1M-context Claude model reads "Opus (1M context)" before Claude Code lists its models. - A Claude Code Code Mode step reads as its script and the calls it made.
## Settings
- Settings has a search field, and ⌘K finds settings too, in English and Korean. - Keyboard shortcuts can be changed in Settings › Keyboard shortcuts. - View › Zoom In, Zoom Out and Actual Size (⌘+, ⌘− and ⌘0) zoom the app's text from 80% to 175%, as in the Codex and Claude apps. - Yardlet follows the Mac's accent color by default. Appearance › Color preset offers the accents Ink, Grove and Iris and the complete palettes Nord, Catppuccin, Ember and Tidepool. The Light and Dark columns can set their own accent, background and text colors, checked for contrast before they are saved, and the interface font can be the system, serif or rounded face. - Changing the language offers Relaunch. - The browser's settings have a Browser section of their own, Harness Accounts and Usage come before Harnesses, and more rows say what they change. - A task's harness settings turn Codex skills and Claude Code plugins on and off through the harness's own commands. They open from Harness settings… in ⌘K, Manage skills… under Codex's Skills, and Claude Code's `/plugin`.
## Tasks
- Sidebar rows stay in place while the pointer is over the list, so a click opens the task you saw. - A message sent into a turn that ended before the agent read it, as when Yardlet quit, goes out again instead of waiting for a turn that never comes. - A task whose harness did not start keeps the message it was started with and the reason in its conversation, and a scheduled run that made it names it. - With no project chosen, the home starts a chat. - A task hears when a subagent it started ends, also after the call returned. - A subagent that ended no longer leaves its calling task waiting on an approval nobody can answer. - A task a schedule started changes other schedules as its permission mode allows, as any task does. - Agents can add a folder as a project with `create_project`. - A sign-in a CLI can no longer renew offers Sign in. - A Claude Code error shows once, as its card. - A Claude Code turn the Mac's sleep cut mid-response is continued. - GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage has its prices.
## Antigravity
- Antigravity CLI tasks run only over ACP. - Antigravity CLI accounts no longer take part in automatic account assignment.
## Browser
- Import from Another Browser… starts with your default browser, and lists the browsers macOS keeps from other apps with how to allow them. - An agent's script on a page gives its task a browser profile of its own only where the page may be signing in, so the task keeps your later sign-ins elsewhere. - Each browser profile's disk cache stays under 80 MiB, and an archived task's profile is removed while the browser keeps running. - A tab shown again no longer stays white until you reload it. - `browser_snapshot` can read one part of a page.
## Another Mac's tasks
- A window for another Mac keeps its close, minimize and zoom buttons on the title bar row as its connection changes. - A task list the other Mac refused is asked for again while the connection stays.
## Faster
- Launch reads saved conversations off the main thread, so a long history no longer stalls "Restoring tasks…". - Hiding and showing the conversation behind an expanded side panel lays out none of its messages. - PDF previews open, draw and close off the main thread. - Long commands and waits on large pages cost the main thread far less.
## Fixes
- A saved file takes the save's modification time, so build tools and file watchers see the change. - A turn you jumped to stays in view when Claude Code's saved conversation replaces the cache. - Codex starts when its account folder's path has a space or a non-ASCII character. - A Codex task that failed to start keeps its first message once its thread starts. - The next Codex task on an account no longer loses its first message after the account's last session closed. - Stopping a Codex turn that had already ended reads as stopped, not failed. - A mail account that could not be read at launch is read again as soon as its watch hears from it. - The calendar sums up each day's recurring runs, so meetings keep their room.

# Yardlet 0.11.12
## Security
- Signing in to a connector asks first when its sign-in page is on another site than the connector's server. The sign-in opens only web pages and takes only its own answer. - Reading another project's tasks through the session tools asks you first, and keys and tokens in what those tools return are hidden. - A task that may only read starts only tasks that may only read. Running or changing a schedule that may do more than the calling task asks you first. - A task's browser takes a profile of its own before an agent runs scripts on a page, and sites in tabs an agent drives ask again for the camera and microphone. - A paired device needs its Terminal permission to start or switch a task to a mode that skips approvals. - Yardlet's folder in your home is private to your account, and the Git that Yardlet runs no longer starts programs a folder's own settings name. - An update no longer installs an older build over a newer one, and a download is checked against the release key before it is opened. - A folder given to a page's file chooser is refused when it holds a link leading outside the task's folders.
## Tasks
- Every task starts on its harness's current CLI, the one chosen in Settings › Harnesses or else the newest install, as the Codex and Claude apps do. Choosing another version moves idle tasks to it with their next message. - Your own message no longer waits behind an account move Yardlet chose itself. Such a move that still waits after ten minutes is given up, and the line above the composer says what a move is waiting for. - Choosing another account for a task with background work waits for that work, as during a turn, instead of ending it. - Background shells and agents keep running after a turn ends on a usage limit or an error. - When every account is nearly spent, automatic assignment picks one with something left before one that is used up. - "Continue with another account" works again after the Claude app updated the CLI it bundles. - A message that reached a task while its CLI was still starting no longer fails with "Claude session is already attached". - A child task's result that its parent task already read no longer counts as needing you in the Dock badge, the menu bar and Next Task Needing Attention. Its unread dot stays in the sidebar. - Next-message suggestions are asked for only in tasks on screen or seen recently, instead of after every turn of every task. - What a CLI writes just before it exits is no longer lost, for Claude Code, ACP agents and Pi. - Disconnecting or removing a connector that runs on this Mac ends everything its server started.
## Claude Code
- Idle compaction (Settings › General › Tasks, on by default) compacts a long Claude Code task that sits idle shortly before its prompt cache expires, by Claude Code's own rules, so coming back after an hour doesn't write the whole conversation to the cache again. - Settings › General › Tasks › Context limit for Claude Code tasks sets the limit for tasks that chose none of their own. The per-task menu adds 600k. - Renaming a task renames its running Claude Code session too, and each session carries its task's title in the list of other sessions Claude Code shows its agents. - Slash commands such as `/compact` read back after a relaunch as they were sent, not as your bubbles with tags.
## Conversation
- A message you send while a turn works now parts the folded work, so the turn reads in the order it happened: the work after your message folds on a "Work details" line under it. - A Claude Code turn you stopped reads "You stopped after N seconds", as a Codex turn does, and the calls the stop cut read Stopped, not failed. - Claude Code's question cards show the previews an option carries (a mockup, code, a draft) beside the options. - An approval card shows the whole command it asks about, scrolling instead of folding. - With the composer empty, Return or ⌘Return allows the oldest waiting tool approval once and Escape denies it, as in the Codex and Claude apps. The card's buttons name their keys. - A Codex command you declined reads "Denied", not "Ran". - Skip on a question card's last question sends on the first click. - Wide tables wrap their cells to fit the message, and a table that still scrolls fades at its edge. Find stays on a match inside a table. - The conversation keeps at least 560 points beside the side panel. Where both don't fit, the panel floats over the conversation's trailing edge. - When a connector tool names a view for its results (MCP Apps), the view shows under the call, in a sandbox of its own ([docs/CONNECTORS.md](https://github.com/zzunkie/yardlet/blob/main/docs/CONNECTORS.md), "MCP Apps"). - A message that starts with a code block draws the block's header and Copy button in place. - Return chooses a typed `/` command even when its list arrived after your last keystroke. - ⌘ shortcuts work under Korean and other non-Latin input sources in the browser panel, the composer's paste, the terminal and the image viewer.
## Settings
- Appearance can choose the font and size for code, diffs, command output, open files and the terminal. - Notifications can choose when a finished or failed turn notifies, whether approvals and questions notify, and the sound. - General › App has Launch at login, off by default. - General › Tasks has Send shortcut: Return, ⌘Return for drafts of several lines, or always ⌘Return, as in the Codex app. - Harness Accounts says each account's limits on one line. Usage keeps the bars and reset times. - Descriptions in Settings are shorter.
## Calendar
- Settings › General › App › Calendar, off by default, shows your connected Google and Outlook calendars and the Mac's calendars beside your tasks, by week or by day, with Yardlet's scheduled runs as a layer of their own. Google and Outlook invitations can be answered there, and an event can be handed to an agent.
## Schedules
- A task's Background tasks card lists the schedules that continue it. - Scheduled tasks groups what will run under Today, Tomorrow, Next 7 days and Later, and names the task a continuing schedule runs in. - A scheduled run's clock lines up with the other marks at the end of its sidebar row.
## Browser and passwords
- Import from Another Browser… is also in the browser panel's ⋯ menu and in Settings › Passwords, and can bring the other browser's visit history into the address field's suggestions. - A sign-in that asks for several secrets, such as an organization's password and then your own, is saved and filled whole. The item sheet shows each secret on a row of its own.
## Antigravity
- Over ACP, the permission menu is the only one: it lists Default, Antigravity's own modes such as Accept edits and Auto, and Bypass permissions. - Bypass permissions runs on Antigravity's own skip-permissions process, so turns Antigravity starts by itself, such as after a subagent ends, no longer wait for an approval. - When an ACP agent such as Antigravity serves several tasks from one process and supports it, closing one task's session tells the agent, so it can release what it started for that session, such as connector servers.
## Another Mac's tasks
- In a window for another Mac that also runs 0.11.12, Review can stage, unstage and discard, and the Files panel can save. Unsaved edits are kept when the window closes. - A terminal keeps running when the window closes or the connection drops, and comes back with its screen when the window opens again.
## Faster
- Scrolling a long conversation or the sidebar does much less work each frame. - A plan limit report redraws only the turn with the limit card, not every turn in view. - Long histories draw with less work on the main thread. - Saving the message queue, the restart record, task profiles, account assignments and model lists no longer holds up the window while the disk is busy.
## Fixes
- A file Yardlet keeps state in and can't read is set aside instead of being written over, and the window says when a save failed. - Queued messages and shell output go out once an edit is cancelled or files are restored, instead of waiting for the next turn. - A task off screen whose message failed to go gets its unread mark and a notification that names the failure. - A schedule moved to continue another task no longer leaves the first task waiting on approval cards. - The Agents card lists a continued Claude Code subagent once. - The main-thread hang log keeps more than a day.
## Thanks
- [@minsujang0](https://github.com/minsujang0) for reporting the per-frame scrolling work in [#677](https://github.com/zzunkie/yardlet/issues/677) and for the scrolling measurements and work in [#719](https://github.com/zzunkie/yardlet/pull/719).
